ROWBOAT BELLOWS AT THE WALL: a leather bellows the size of a rowboat wedged hard against the stone, its timber arms raised high, plain iron bands strapping its ribs, its nozzle sunk into the wall at an uneven angle, one strap fraying at the buckle

THREE BELLOWS OF DIFFERENT SIZES: three leather bellows hung at different heights on iron pegs, the largest sagging open at the seam, the middle one patched with a darker hide, the smallest hooked well away from the others on a peg set into a crack in the wall

BELLOWS ON THE SHAFT STRAP: a broad leather bellows linked by a long leather strap to a turning shaft set into the wall, the strap riding an off-centre wooden pulley, the bellows rocking unevenly with each rotation of the shaft

HAND BELLOWS BY THE STONE: a small hand bellows leaning at a tilt against the stone, its wooden handles worn smooth, its leather worn pale at the fold, a length of cord looped once around the near handle

BELLOWS WEDGED IN THE LOW ARCH: a leather bellows of middling size wedged into a low side arch, its timber arms propped open by a short iron rod, its nozzle angled down toward the floor grate, one arm cracked and bound with a strip of hide

WHEEL IN THE DARK RACE: a wooden wheel turning slowly in a race of dark water cut through the floor, its paddles dripping, worn smooth on one edge where they strike the stone lip, water trailing back into shadow along the cut channel

LONG SHAFT DOWN THE HALL: a long timber shaft running the full length of the hall at shoulder height, set in plain iron collars bolted to timber posts of uneven spacing, three leather drive straps hanging off it at different intervals, one strap longer than the others and coiled on the floor beneath

CLUSTER OF WOODEN COGS: a cluster of wooden cogs of three different sizes sitting in a timber cradle on the floor, their teeth cut at different pitches, the largest cog tilted slightly off the cradle's edge, a mallet resting across the top of the middle cog

SPARE PADDLE WHEEL AGAINST THE WALL: a second wooden wheel leaning at an angle against the wall near the race, two of its paddles replaced with timber of a lighter colour, a rope looped around its hub and tied to an iron ring set into the stone

CRUCIBLE ON THE SWING ARM: a crucible cradled in a plain iron ring mounted on a swing arm, the arm extended out over the floor at a slight angle, a chain keeping it from swinging further, the crucible's outer wall darkened and rough

LONG-HANDLED LADLE AT THE STONE LIP: a long-handled ladle resting across a low stone lip, its bowl tipped toward the floor, the handle worn lighter at the grip, a loop of iron wire twisted around the handle's end for hanging

BED OF SAND MOULDS: a bed of sand moulds pressed into a shallow timber-edged frame on the floor, the shapes rough and of uneven depth, three moulds already poured and set apart at one end, the rest still open and waiting

TIPPING CRADLE OVER THE MOULD BED: a tipping cradle of iron and timber standing on splayed legs over a mould bed, its pivot pin set off-centre so the cradle tips more easily to the right, a length of chain hanging from one side to slow the pour

CHAIN HOIST ON THE BEAM: a chain hoist hanging from a timber beam off to one side of the hall, its great hook turning slowly on the last link, the chain looped once around a wooden cleat nailed to the beam, a short length of rope tied to the hook for guiding

COUNTERWEIGHT OF STACKED STONE: a counterweight of three flat stones stacked unevenly on a timber platform, a rope running up from the platform over a plain iron pulley set into the beam, the rope descending on the far side to a hook at working height

SET OF CHAINS AT UNEVEN LENGTHS: a set of five chains hanging from a single iron ring bolted to the beam, each chain a different length, the hooks at their ends resting at different heights, the longest chain looped once at the bottom to keep it off the floor

TIMBER CRANE ARM OVER THE FLOOR: a timber crane arm mounted on a turning post set into the floor to one side, swung out over the open floor at an angle, a rope and plain hook hanging from its end, a wooden wedge driven under the post to hold it at that angle

TIPPED CART AT THE RAMP FOOT: a small iron-bound cart tipped on its side at the foot of a stone ramp, broken ore spilled in a rough heap around it, the cart's single wheel still turning slowly, one iron band on the rim bent outward

BLACK STONE CHUTE AND ORE HEAP: a chute of dark stone set at a steep angle into the wall, broken ore spilling from its mouth into a heap on the floor, the heap uneven and spread further to the left, a few pieces of ore rolled well away from the main pile

BARROW HALF FULL AND LEFT: a wooden barrow resting where it was left in the middle of the floor, its handles dropped to the ground, half full of broken ore and rough stone, one handle cracked and wrapped tight with a strip of leather

TIMBER STACK AND CHARCOAL BASKET: a stack of split timber leaning against the wall in an uneven pile, the pieces of different lengths, a wicker basket of charcoal sitting apart from the stack with one handle broken and tied back with twine

LONG STONE TROUGH WITH PLANK LID: a long stone trough of dark water running along the wall, its plank lid pushed aside and resting at an angle across the near end, the water still, the stone sides of the trough darkened and smooth at the lip from long use

GRINDSTONE ON THE TIMBER FRAME: a great grindstone sitting in a timber frame set to one side, its treadle worn dark and smooth, the stone slightly off-centre on its axle, a small wooden peg driven into the frame to keep the treadle from swinging too far back

RACK OF TONGS AND HAMMERS: a rack of plain iron tongs and hammers of uneven lengths hanging on iron pegs set into the wall at different heights, the handles worn to different degrees, one hammer hung apart from the rest on a peg set into a crack lower down

LOW STONE BENCH WITH PUNCHES AND CHISELS: a low stone bench worn smooth across its top from long use, punches and chisels of different lengths scattered across it at odd angles, a few pushed to the far end in a loose cluster, one punch fallen to the floor beside the bench leg
